correctness.rationale: For a finite ordinal sum of antichains each of size at least two, bounded morphism maps each source antichain to a single target level: otherwise equation f(up x)=up f(x) conflicts with the at-least-two elements of an intervening target level. The nondecreasing target-level sequence visits every level above the first; no such higher level can be visited twice, because comparability forces a singleton image whereas the image is an upset. It follows that exactly one of the two asserted normal forms holds, and conversely both satisfy the back-lifting identity. Finite Esakia duality turns these into all Heyting endomorphisms. Direct counting of transformations, surjections by image size, and idempotent maps yields all formulas. Exhaustive independent finite enumeration over nine vectors verified the bounded-morphism condition, exact image ranks, idempotence, and direct implication preservation for small carriers; analytic proof covers arbitrary heights. Singleton-level exclusion is essential.

value.rationale: The finite Boolean cascades form a classical natural family of finite Heyting algebras important for weak Pierce logic. The result classifies every implication-preserving self-map for arbitrarily many nonsingleton levels, proving that all upper levels are either rigidly permuted or removed by a single initial collapse. It supplies a full, collision-free image-rank distribution and idempotent/retraction census, structurally refining ordinary subalgebra or automorphism counts. These invariants encode possible homomorphic images and retracts and are not arbitrary small enumerations. The central rigidity lemma and exact spectrum are mathematically meaningful even without a downstream theorem.
